title: Execute rounded Gaussian words against shared finite-core references
body:
I connect the retained Gaussian carve, raw interior circuits and rounded boundary solver into complete ordinary finite-core narrow inverse and broad forward programs. I derive each Schur page from the same exact rational reference, retain the original couplings and six-call order, and execute with one grid and an explicit intermediate-input budget. The broad program applies its Schur factor; the narrow program consumes prepared rounded inverse pages through the retained block/Strassen arithmetic.

For maximum complex-l1 input bound `Y0`, five-factor norm bound `K` and target `2^-t`, I take `Y*=6K^5Y0` and local error `e=2^-t/(10K^4)`. I prove complete error at most `2^(-t-1)`, supply a reference allocation before window selection and bound arithmetic temporaries. `CORE-PROOF.md` states the hypotheses and residual argument. I preserve the six earlier FFT, triangular, generator, full Toeplitz, normalized Gaussian and raw-reference receipts.

I check four finite-core cases: two 143-row programs with two 16-row interiors each, and two 11-row windows crossing a hole. They execute 88,704 dense gate applications and 19,992 boundary scalar products. I check each stage against its actual input, complete narrow residuals and broad products, a 768-bit incoming grid, prepared-page equivalence and 13 controls. The core scientific digest is `65f0cefaed8d7b8b21125cde5155401b3880e896b49068e8e8c86895b5004e4d`.

Reproduce with CPython 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/rational-unitary-fft
```

I declare eight normal/optimized commands with a total timeout budget of 1,200 seconds. I run the full, normalized, raw and core checks sequentially in the final two commands.

I passed all eight registered checks and all eight Git-free checks at head `78c72e563173f3822fcb4efed9ceeccf05630258`. I checked 63 committed payload files and their source-history pins; all 64 exported files stayed unchanged. The combined export commands took 147.066 and 146.018 seconds. Archive SHA256: `dca7449c8bbd870be87655373969d940dc42af69ed40da632873ae1105ad907e`; receipt SHA256: `2b0882f33e7480cef5c713f96ba83a663137fc04504190db402d1aa3f6b3319e`.

I matched all fourteen scientific records and seven receipt digests from the successful [hosted run39492372797](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39492372797) to the export. GitHub also passed the unchanged-input check. I verified test merge `7acbb956f35751735f0948e6c751787b8635ad4c`, its exact base/head parents and publication tree `d069aea846216a42c32d1761c2e356719b2c7e16`.

The finite fixtures use cap 16 with physical half-band 18; I make no large-cap scaling claim from them. I keep exact Schur/LU/inverse preparation outside online counts. Core/halo comparison, cyclic corners, tensor composition, physical coefficient delivery and complete tape/setup costs remain open. Reviewers still need to assess the quantified proofs. I claim no new selected exponent or complete multiplication theorem.

I credit Vlado Vojdanovski for the retained circuits, carve, factor order and block/Strassen program; Jeremy Kothe/IdeaOuter for shifted Gaussian identities; Mason Hale for interval arithmetic; Chafik Boukhalfa for certified phases; and Cinna Davis for the later caller. I retain our PR4186 boundary adapter with its original provenance. ToikY's PR4209 Schur theorem and PR4220 independent scalar audit, Nick Petalas's PR4217 HALO audit and James Reed's limited budget/source checks retain their separate scopes. Internal analysis agents belong to our author process.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematics, implementation and writing. Apache-2.0.
